items.title: 🧠 Stixflayer 🦑
items.text:
Rust-native STIX 2.1. One spec-compliant core, consumed by many. ⚡

Parse, validate, and serialize at 10–40× the speed of the industry-standard Python validator — with stricter spec enforcement.

  • 🚀 Quickstart

    Parse a document, build an object, handle errors — in five minutes.

    Get started

  • 📖 Guides

    Parsing, building, validation modes, vocabularies, patterns, errors.

    Browse the guides

  • 📚 API reference

    Curated reference for every public class and function.

    Open the reference

  • 🦀 Rust

    The native crate, documented where Rust users expect it.

    Rust docs.rs/stixflayer

items.title: Why another STIX library? 🤔
items.text:
• 🌍 One engine, no validation gaps — most STIX libraries are reimplemented per language, so the same document can be valid in one and rejected in another. stixflayer ships a single Rust core into every language, so data validates the same way everywhere.
  • ⚔️ Battle-tested, but faster — built from OASIS's reference implementation, with full parity against the industry-standard validator, at 10–40× the speed.
  • 🧐 Stricter where it matters — rejects empty bundles, invalid vocabulary values, and incorrect SCO UUIDv5 hashes that other validators skip.

items.title: Performance 🚀
items.text: Operation stix2-validator stixflayer speedup Parse + validate apt1 bundle ~47 ms ~1.6 ms ~30× 🏎️ Parse + validate poisonivy bundle ~99 ms ~2.3 ms ~40× 🏎️ Serialize apt1 bundle ~0.6 ms ~0.06 ms ~10× 🏎️ Serialize poisonivy bundle ~1.0 ms ~0.09 ms ~12× 🏎️

items.title: Install ⚡
items.text:
pip install stixflayer

Requires Python 3.11+. Rust users: cargo add stixflayer 🦀 — API docs at docs.rs/stixflayer.

items.title: Credits 🙏
items.text: Built on OASIS CTI's cti-rust-stix, the official STIX 2.1 reference implementation in Rust, and benchmarked against cti-stix-validator.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text: Install stixflayer, parse a STIX 2.1 document, and handle validation errors. Every code block on this page is executed in CI — what you see is what it prints.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install stixflayer

Requires Python 3.11 or newer. Rust users: cargo add stixflayer, with the API reference on docs.rs.

items.title: Parse and validate a document
items.text:
Parsing validates: a document that fails STIX 2.1 rules is rejected at from_json, not silently accepted.

import json

from stixflayer import Bundle

document = json.dumps(
    {
        "type": "bundle",
        "id": "bundle--0c7b5d88-7c1c-4a8b-8f0c-6e9d4f2b1a55",
        "objects": [
            {
                "type": "attack-pattern",
                "spec_version": "2.1",
                "id": "attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
                "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
                "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
                "name": "Clear Command History",
            },
            {
                "type": "indicator",
                "spec_version": "2.1",
                "id": "indicator--a924e94c-4d7d-4f9a-9c9e-2b0f8f4b9f1d",
                "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
                "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
                "name": "Malicious IP",
                "pattern": "[ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7']",
                "pattern_type": "stix",
                "valid_from": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
            },
        ],
    }
)

bundle = Bundle.from_json(document)
print(bundle.object_count)
#> 2
for obj in bundle.objects:
    print(obj.type, obj.id)
    #> attack-pattern attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830
    #> indicator indicator--a924e94c-4d7d-4f9a-9c9e-2b0f8f4b9f1d

items.title: Build an object
items.text:
Build STIX Domain Objects directly or with builders. Required properties are enforced on construction.

from stixflayer import AttackPattern

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    description="Adversaries clear or remove bash_history to hide their tracks.",
    spec_version="2.1",
)
print(ap.name)
#> Clear Command History

items.title: Handle validation errors
items.text:
Failures raise a structured exception — every error carries a machine-readable errors list, not just a message.

from stixflayer import AttackPattern, ValidationError

try:
    AttackPattern.from_json(
        '{"type": "attack-pattern", "spec_version": "2.1", "id": "attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830", "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z", "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z"}'
    )
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.errors[0]["kind"], e.errors[0]["property"])
    #> missing_property name

items.title: Cyber-observables
items.text:
All classes below share the common interface. SCOs are identified by deterministic UUIDv5 identifiers derived from their content — you never supply an id when constructing one.

from stixflayer import IPv4Address

ip = IPv4Address(value="203.0.113.7")
print(ip.type, ip.id)
#> ipv4-addr ipv4-addr--9ddd739e-87b1-587d-83f2-62ef1130af2f

items.title: Deterministic identifiers
items.text:
The same observable always produces the same identifier — useful for deduplication across feeds.

from stixflayer import DomainName

a = DomainName(value="example.com")
b = DomainName(value="example.com")
print(a.id == b.id)
#> True

items.title: Domain objects
items.text: All classes below share the common interface: keyword construction, from_json, to_json, and typed property accessors.

items.title: STIX Domain Objects (SDOs)
items.text:
Class Required name property AttackPattern name Campaign name CourseOfAction name Grouping context, object_refs Identity name Incident name Indicator name, pattern, pattern_type, valid_from Infrastructure name IntrusionSet name Location — Malware name, is_family MalwareAnalysis product, version Note content, object_refs ObservedData objects, first_observed, last_observed, number_observed Opinion opinion, object_refs Report name, published, object_refs ThreatActor name Tool name Vulnerability name 
from stixflayer import ThreatActor

ta = ThreatActor(
    id="threat-actor--0ab1f132-d6c5-4d4f-a0e3-ff9bda992932",
    name="Foobar",
    spec_version="2.1",
    created="2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
    modified="2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
    threat_actor_types=["crime-syndicate"],
)
print(ta.name)
#> Foobar

items.text:
Class Notes Relationship Connects two objects via relationship_type Sighting Records that an object was seen 
from stixflayer import Relationship

rel = Relationship(
    id="relationship--0b1c2d3e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e",
    spec_version="2.1",
    created="2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
    modified="2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
    relationship_type="uses",
    source_ref="threat-actor--0ab1f132-d6c5-4d4f-a0e3-ff9bda992932",
    target_ref="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
)
print(rel.relationship_type)
#> uses

items.title: Meta objects
items.text: Class Purpose MarkingDefinition Data marking / handling labels ExtensionDefinition Defines a STIX extension LanguageContent Language-specific content for an object

items.title: Bundles and custom objects
items.text:
Class Purpose Bundle Container of STIX objects; rejects empty bundles CustomObject User-defined object types (new-sdo / new-sco / new-sro) 
from stixflayer import AttackPattern, Bundle

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    spec_version="2.1",
    created="2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
    modified="2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
)
bundle = Bundle(objects=[ap])
bundle.add(ap.to_json())
print(bundle.object_count)
#> 2

items.title: Exceptions
items.text: All errors derive from StixError. Every error carries a structured errors list — see error handling for the catalog of entry kinds and fields.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text:
StixError
├── ValidationError      # parses, but violates STIX 2.1 rules
└── DeserializationError # cannot be parsed as STIX JSON

from stixflayer import DeserializationError, StixError, ValidationError

print(issubclass(ValidationError, StixError))
#> True
print(issubclass(DeserializationError, StixError))
#> True

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Type Present on errors list[dict] Every StixError — at least one entry with kind and message args[0] str Human-readable message

items.title: Typical handling
items.text:
import json

from stixflayer import AttackPattern, DeserializationError, ValidationError

bad_json = '{"type": "attack-pattern"'  # truncated — not valid JSON
not_stix = json.dumps({"hello": "world"})

for payload in (bad_json, not_stix):
    try:
        AttackPattern.from_json(payload)
    except DeserializationError as e:
        print("cannot parse:", type(e).__name__)
        #> cannot parse: DeserializationError
    except ValidationError as e:
        print("parsed, invalid:", e.errors[0]["kind"])
        #> parsed, invalid: missing_property

items.title: validate_pattern(pattern)
items.text:
Validates a STIX pattern. Returns silently if valid; raises ValidationError with an invalid_pattern entry if not.

import stixflayer

stixflayer.validate_pattern("[ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7']")

try:
    stixflayer.validate_pattern("[ipv4-addr:value = 203.0.113.7]")
except Exception as e:
    print(e.errors[0]["kind"])
    #> invalid_pattern

items.title: version()
items.text:
Returns the stixflayer version.

import stixflayer

print(stixflayer.version())
#> 0.1.0

items.title: API overview
items.text: Everything is importable from the top-level package. The full type surface is declared in type stubs, so IDEs and type checkers resolve all of it.

items.title: What's in the box
items.text: Group Members Reference Exceptions StixError, ValidationError, DeserializationError Exceptions Functions version(), validate_pattern() Functions Domain objects 19 SDO classes (AttackPattern, Identity, Malware, …) Domain objects Relationship objects Relationship, Sighting Domain objects Meta objects MarkingDefinition, ExtensionDefinition, LanguageContent Domain objects Cyber-observables 18 SCO classes (File, IPv4Address, NetworkTraffic, …) Cyber-observables Vocabularies 8 enum classes (.values(), .is_valid()) Vocabularies Bundles & custom Bundle, CustomObject Domain objects

items.title: Shared behavior
items.text:
All SDO and SCO classes share the same interface:

  • Class(**properties) — construct; required properties enforced
  • Class.from_json(json_str, strict=True, allow_custom=False) — parse and validate
  • obj.to_json() — serialize back to STIX 2.1 JSON
  • obj.type, obj.id, obj.spec_version — common properties
  • obj.custom_properties — properties outside the specification
  • Typed accessors for standard properties; unknown attributes raise AttributeError

See validation modes for strict and allow_custom semantics, and error handling for the structured error entries.

items.title: Vocabularies
items.text:
Enum-like classes for STIX open vocabularies. Every class supports the same interface.

Class STIX vocabulary AttackMotivation attack-motivation-ov AttackResourceLevel attack-resource-level-ov IdentitySectors identity-sector-ov IndicatorType indicator-type-ov MalwareType malware-type-ov ReportType report-type-ov ThreatActorSophistication threat-actor-sophistication-ov ThreatActorType threat-actor-type-ov

items.title: Interface
items.text:
Member Description Class(value) Construct from a string; invalid values raise Class.values() All valid values, as list[str] Class.is_valid(value) True/False without raising .value() The string value of an instance 
from stixflayer import ThreatActorSophistication

sophistication = ThreatActorSophistication("advanced")
print(sophistication.value())
#> advanced
print(ThreatActorSophistication.is_valid("advanced"))
#> True
print(ThreatActorSophistication.is_valid("bogus"))
#> False

Object fields that use a vocabulary accept plain strings and are validated on construction — see vocabularies guide.

items.title: Building objects
items.text: Construct STIX objects directly with keyword arguments. Required properties are enforced on construction — you cannot build an invalid object by accident.

items.title: Domain objects
items.text:
from stixflayer import AttackPattern

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    description="Adversaries clear or remove bash_history to hide their tracks.",
    spec_version="2.1",
)
print(ap.name)
#> Clear Command History

Missing required properties raise ValidationError immediately:

from stixflayer import AttackPattern, ValidationError

try:
    AttackPattern(
        id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
        spec_version="2.1",
    )
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.errors[0]["kind"], e.errors[0]["property"])
    #> missing_property name

items.title: Cyber-observable objects
items.text:
SCOs get their deterministic UUIDv5 identifier from their content — you never supply an id.

from stixflayer import IPv4Address

ip = IPv4Address(value="203.0.113.7")
print(ip.type, ip.id)
#> ipv4-addr ipv4-addr--9ddd739e-87b1-587d-83f2-62ef1130af2f

items.title: Custom properties
items.text:
Standard objects accept properties outside the specification with allow_custom=True. They are readable as attributes and collected in custom_properties.

from stixflayer import AttackPattern

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    description="Adversaries clear or remove bash_history to hide their tracks.",
    spec_version="2.1",
    allow_custom=True,
    x_mitre_detection="Monitor command history",
)
print(ap.x_mitre_detection)
#> Monitor command history
print(ap.custom_properties)
#> {'x_mitre_detection': 'Monitor command history'}

items.title: User-defined object types
items.text:
For objects with a custom type, use CustomObject with extension_type set to new-sdo, new-sco, or new-sro depending on what it extends.

from stixflayer import CustomObject

co = CustomObject(
    type_="x-example-thing",
    extension_type="new-sco",
    name="Example",
    version=2,
)
print(co.type, co.name)
#> x-example-thing Example

items.title: Error handling
items.text:
Two exceptions cover every failure. Both carry a structured errors list — never just a string.

from stixflayer import DeserializationError, StixError, ValidationError

print(issubclass(ValidationError, StixError))
#> True
print(issubclass(DeserializationError, StixError))
#> True
Exception Raised when DeserializationError Input is not parseable as STIX JSON — malformed JSON, wrong types, or not a JSON object ValidationError The JSON parses but violates STIX 2.1 rules — missing properties, unknown properties, bad vocabulary values, invalid patterns

Both are subclasses of StixError, so except StixError catches everything.

items.title: Anatomy of an error entry
items.text:
Every entry has a kind and a human-readable message. Most kinds add contextual fields, so you can branch on structured data instead of parsing messages.

from stixflayer import Identity, ValidationError

try:
    Identity(
        id="identity--c78b4a5a-3b42-4f2e-9b1a-7f8e9d0c1a2b",
        name="Acme Corp",
        spec_version="2.1",
        created="2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
        modified="2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
        identity_class="bogus-class",
    )
except ValidationError as e:
    entry = e.errors[0]
    print(entry["kind"], "|", entry["vocabulary"], "|", entry["value"])
    #> invalid_vocab_value | identity-class-ov | bogus-class

items.title: Error catalog
items.text: Kind Extra fields Meaning missing_property property A required property is absent unknown_property properties Property names outside the specification invalid_property_type property, expected, got A property has the wrong JSON type invalid_vocab_value value, vocabulary Value not in its STIX vocabulary invalid_hash value, expected, got Hash value doesn't match its algorithm invalid_timestamp value Timestamp not in STIX 2.1 format invalid_identifier value Malformed STIX identifier invalid_pattern value, got STIX pattern fails to parse empty_list — A list property or bundle contains no items deserialization_error — Catch-all for input that can't be deserialized

items.title: Catching by failure type
items.text:
JSON that can't be understood at all raises DeserializationError — including JSON that parses but isn't a STIX object.

from stixflayer import DeserializationError, Identity

try:
    Identity.from_json("[1, 2, 3]")
except DeserializationError as e:
    print(e)
    #> Deserialization error: Expected a STIX object (JSON object), got array.

items.title: Pattern errors
items.text:
Invalid STIX patterns raise ValidationError with an invalid_pattern entry carrying the pattern and the parse failure.

import stixflayer

try:
    stixflayer.validate_pattern("[ipv4-addr:value = 192.0.2.1]")
except Exception as e:
    entry = e.errors[0]
    print(entry["kind"], "|", entry["value"])
    #> invalid_pattern | [ipv4-addr:value = 192.0.2.1]

items.title: Parsing and validation
items.text: stixflayer parses STIX 2.1 JSON and validates it in one step: from_json returns a live object or raises — there is no separate validate call to forget.

items.title: Load a bundle
items.text:
import json

from stixflayer import Bundle

document = json.dumps(
    {
        "type": "bundle",
        "id": "bundle--0c7b5d88-7c1c-4a8b-8f0c-6e9d4f2b1a55",
        "objects": [
            {
                "type": "attack-pattern",
                "spec_version": "2.1",
                "id": "attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
                "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
                "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
                "name": "Clear Command History",
            },
        ],
    }
)

bundle = Bundle.from_json(document)
print(bundle.object_count)
#> 1
for obj in bundle.objects:
    print(obj.type, obj.id)
    #> attack-pattern attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830

bundle.objects contains live Python objects with typed accessors, not raw dictionaries — unknown attributes raise AttributeError.

items.title: Load a single object
items.text:
Every object class has a from_json constructor.

from stixflayer import IPv4Address

ip = IPv4Address.from_json(
    '{"type": "ipv4-addr", "id": "ipv4-addr--9ddd739e-87b1-587d-83f2-62ef1130af2f", "value": "203.0.113.7"}'
)
print(ip.value, ip.id)
#> 203.0.113.7 ipv4-addr--9ddd739e-87b1-587d-83f2-62ef1130af2f

items.title: Round-trip to JSON
items.text:
to_json serializes back to STIX 2.1 JSON.

import json

from stixflayer import AttackPattern

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    description="Adversaries clear or remove bash_history to hide their tracks.",
    spec_version="2.1",
)
roundtrip = json.loads(ap.to_json())
print(roundtrip["type"], roundtrip["name"])
#> attack-pattern Clear Command History

items.title: Invalid input raises
items.text:
Documents that break STIX 2.1 rules — or aren't STIX JSON at all — raise before you get an object. See validation modes and error handling for what comes back and how to handle it.

from stixflayer import Bundle

try:
    Bundle.from_json('{"type": "bundle", "id": "bundle--0c7b5d88-7c1c-4a8b-8f0c-6e9d4f2b1a55"}')
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)
    #> DeserializationError

items.title: STIX patterns
items.text: Validate STIX patterns without building any object.

items.title: Validate a pattern
items.text:
validate_pattern returns silently for a valid pattern.

import stixflayer

stixflayer.validate_pattern("[ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7']")

items.title: Invalid patterns raise
items.text:
Syntactically invalid patterns raise ValidationError with an invalid_pattern entry — the pattern itself plus a plain-language parse failure.

import stixflayer

try:
    stixflayer.validate_pattern("[ipv4-addr:value = 203.0.113.7]")
except Exception as e:
    entry = e.errors[0]
    print(entry["kind"])
    #> invalid_pattern
    print(entry["got"])
    #> expected a specific character near '[ipv4-addr:value = 203.0.113.7]'

items.title: Composite patterns
items.text:
Comparisons, AND/OR/NOT, and multiple observations are all supported.

import stixflayer

stixflayer.validate_pattern("[network-traffic:src_port = 22 AND network-traffic:dst_port = 443]")

items.title: Validation modes
items.text: stixflayer validates by default. Two options control how lenient parsing and construction are: allow_custom for custom properties, and strict for spec conformance checks.

items.title: What is always enforced
items.text:
Required properties are enforced in every mode — an object missing name never passes, strict or not.

import json

from stixflayer import AttackPattern

incomplete = json.dumps(
    {
        "type": "attack-pattern",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": "attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
        "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
        "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
    }
)
try:
    AttackPattern.from_json(incomplete)
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)
    #> ValidationError

items.title: Custom properties: allow_custom
items.text:
Properties outside the STIX 2.1 specification are rejected by default. Pass allow_custom=True to accept them.

from stixflayer import AttackPattern

ap = AttackPattern(
    id="attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
    name="Clear Command History",
    description="Adversaries clear or remove bash_history to hide their tracks.",
    spec_version="2.1",
    allow_custom=True,
    x_mitre_detection="Monitor command history",
)
print(ap.x_mitre_detection)
#> Monitor command history

items.title: Spec conformance: strict
items.text:
With strict=True (the default), values are checked against the STIX vocabularies. With strict=False, those conformance checks are skipped — useful for processing incomplete or non-conformant data you cannot fix.

from stixflayer import Identity, ValidationError

kwargs = dict(
    id="identity--c78b4a5a-3b42-4f2e-9b1a-7f8e9d0c1a2b",
    name="Acme Corp",
    spec_version="2.1",
    created="2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
    modified="2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
)

try:
    Identity(identity_class="bogus-class", **kwargs)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.errors[0]["kind"], e.errors[0]["value"])
    #> invalid_vocab_value bogus-class

lenient = Identity(identity_class="bogus-class", strict=False, **kwargs)
print(lenient.identity_class)
#> bogus-class

items.title: All errors at once
items.text:
Validation collects every problem it finds — inspect errors as a list instead of fixing one error per attempt.

import json

from stixflayer import AttackPattern, ValidationError

document = json.dumps(
    {
        "type": "attack-pattern",
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": "attack-pattern--d3046a90-580c-4004-8208-66915bc29830",
        "created": "2019-04-24T15:12:36.609Z",
        "modified": "2023-03-24T15:14:15.637Z",
        "bogus_property": "x",
    }
)
try:
    AttackPattern.from_json(document)
except ValidationError as e:
    print([entry["kind"] for entry in e.errors])
    #> ['unknown_property', 'missing_property']

See error handling for the full error catalog.

items.title: Vocabularies
items.text: STIX defines open vocabularies for fields like threat actor types and industries. stixflayer exposes each as an enum-like class that validates values and lists what's allowed.

items.title: Check and list values
items.text:
from stixflayer import IdentitySectors, ThreatActorSophistication

print(ThreatActorSophistication.values())
#> ['advanced', 'expert', 'innovator', 'intermediate', 'none', 'minimal', 'strategic']
print(IdentitySectors.is_valid("technology"))
#> True

items.title: Use a vocabulary value
items.text:
Vocabulary fields on objects accept plain strings and are validated on construction — an invalid value raises with the vocabulary name and the rejected value.

from stixflayer import Identity, ValidationError

try:
    Identity(
        id="identity--c78b4a5a-3b42-4f2e-9b1a-7f8e9d0c1a2b",
